Definition: properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (3037 being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called:--sardius.
BiblicalUsage: The sardius is the red gem set twice in Revelation: once beside the jasper in the likeness of the One on the throne, and once as the sixth stone in the foundations of the New Jerusalem's wall.
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from this is that the same stone frames both the throne and the city — the King and His people are set in the same jewels.
